statements.label: cor:witness
statements.statement: For a faulting input, conditions (F3) and (F5) may be replaced by a certificate field naming one g_x S _x that precedes every selected barrier. Every valid leaf admits such a witness, and any such witness supplies all existential predecessors required by (F5).

statements.label: thm:waiting
statements.statement: On full permutations of a fixed action set, the legality languages of finite snapshot-action models are exactly the languages defined by finite families of canonical waiting conditions.

statements.label: prop:nonposet
statements.statement: The three-action model of Figure~ admits exactly abz,azb,baz,bza . No directed acyclic graph on \ a,b,z\ has exactly those topological orders. Three is the smallest action count for a nonempty full-permutation legality language with this property.

statements.label: thm:unique
statements.statement: Suppose every faulting input in a cell C has exactly one acceptable representative, | _x|=1 . Let Q be the union of all source-prefix identities and all unique representatives. If any valid leaf exists, restricting its order to Q remains valid. Consequently Q is the unique inclusion-least feasible identity set, and minimum positive additive cost reduces to acyclicity and topological ordering of ordinary precedence constraints on Q .

statements.label: thm:hard
statements.statement: For the unbounded mathematical family, deciding whether a valid branchless leaf with at most k selected actions exists is NP-complete, even when all guards are true, there are no emissions, all action costs are one, there is one observed fault signature, and every input has exactly two acceptable representatives.

statements.label: lem:completion
statements.statement: If is a valid leaf, appending any ordering of any omitted identities preserves validity. Consequently, a valid selected leaf exists if and only if a valid full permutation exists.

statements.label: lem:sparse
statements.statement: Let P be the union of source-prefix identities over a cell. In any valid leaf, let f_x be its first enabled fault on each faulting input. Restricting the leaf to \[ Q=P \ f_x : x faults \ \] preserves validity. If two faulting inputs have the same good set, their retained first faults are equal. Therefore every inclusion-minimal valid leaf has at most |P|+d identities, where d is the number of distinct good sets in the cell.

statements.label: thm:representatives
statements.statement: For every distinct good set G , choose one representative f_G G and form Q_f=P \ f_G\ . The minimum positive additive leaf cost equals the minimum feasible cost among these representative selections. If M contains P and all singleton representatives, complete search may enumerate either all subsets of R M added to M , or all tuples over distinct non-singleton good sets. The smaller candidate bound is \[ (2^ |R M| ,\ _ G:\,|G|>1 |G| ). \]

statements.label: thm:checker
statements.statement: If a well-formed model, canonical decoded object, and certificate pass the checker at external budget B , the object has at most B bytes and is observationally equivalent to the source for every input. Conversely, every valid canonical object of at most B bytes admits a passing certificate.

statements.label: prop:monotone
statements.statement: Every target valid under a refined observer is valid under the coarser observer after projecting its terminal signature. Therefore the refined minimum size is no smaller than the coarse minimum in the same grammar.

statements.label: thm:gap
